sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the notification center
sections.what: Brings in the React tools, icons, the popup pieces, the notification row, the button, the style helper, and the shared API client. Nothing appears on screen from this section.
sections.why: The center needs these pieces to load and show notifications.

sections.name: formatRelativeTime
sections.title: Friendly relative time
sections.what: Turns a timestamp into a short phrase: 'Just now' under a minute, then minutes, hours, or days ago. If the timestamp cannot be read, it shows 'Recent'.
sections.why: Shows notification ages in a short, easy-to-scan form.
sections.watch_out: The phrase is calculated once when the row draws, so it will not update on its own while the popup stays open.

sections.name: mapDbTypeToUiType
sections.title: Server type to display type mapping
sections.what: Converts the server's type names into the app's notification types. Reminder stays reminder, alert and escalation both become alert, system stays system, and anything else becomes info.
sections.why: Connects the server's naming to the display look used by the notification row.
sections.watch_out: A new server type name that is not listed here will quietly show as info, which can hide an important alert.

sections.name: NotificationCenter (part 1)
sections.title: Loading and marking notifications read
sections.what: Fetches the notification history from the server when the bell first appears and again every 30 seconds. It converts each server record into the shape the bell uses, then counts unread items for the badge. It also provides the actions that mark one notification or all notifications as read, updating the screen first and then telling the server.
sections.why: The 30 second repeat keeps the bell badge close to current without the user reloading. Updating the screen before the server call makes the bell feel instant. Reason for the optimistic order is not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: If the server call fails, the screen still shows the item as read until the next refresh, so the displayed state can differ from the server. The polling timer runs whenever the page is open, even when the bell is closed.

sections.name: NotificationCenter (part 2)
sections.title: Filtering and the notification popover header
sections.what: Keeps only the notifications that match the chosen tab, then draws the bell button with an unread count and the popover header with mark-all-read and settings buttons.
sections.why: Likely reason: the unread count sits on the bell and in the header so the count is always visible.
sections.watch_out: The AI tab matches any title containing the letters ai, so unrelated words such as mail can appear under it.

sections.name: NotificationCenter (part 3)
sections.title: Tabs, notification list, and footer
sections.what: Draws the All, AI and Updates tabs, then the list of notification cards. While first loading it shows a spinner, and when the list is empty it shows an all caught up message. A Refresh button sits at the bottom.
sections.why: Likely reason: the loading and empty messages tell the user what state the list is in.
sections.watch_out: The spinner only appears when the list is empty, so a refresh with existing items gives no sign that it is loading.

summary: The notification panel that loads alerts from the server and shows them in a popup list, based on the visible parts of this file.
purpose: Lets the user open a popup and see recent notifications, with the times shown in a friendly format.
why: Keeps notifications in one place. Reason for the full design is not fully visible because only part of the file is in this packet.
how: The helpers turn a timestamp into a phrase like '5m ago' and convert the server's notification type names into the app's type names. The rest of the file, which is not in this packet, handles loading the list, the popup, and the mark-all-read action.
inputs: Notification records from the server through the shared API client, and timestamps and type names inside them.
outputs: A popup with a list of notifications and a count, based on the parts visible here.
risks: Unknown server type names fall back to the generic info style. An invalid date shows 'Recent' rather than a real time. Most of the file's behavior is not visible in this packet.
debug: If times look wrong, check the timestamp passed to the time helper. If a notification has the wrong look, check the type mapping. For the rest of the behavior, check the sections that are not in this packet.
